prompt.en: Bare profession is not the point; faith has to be ____ under trial.

explanation.en: The essay sets mere profession against real faith: saying 'We have faith' is not the point, because faith has to be proven under trial. So the missing word is 'proven.'

anchor.quote: Bare profession is not the point; faith has to be proven under trial.

prompt.en: "So the meeting here is not seeing Him with the eye; the meeting is the resurrection." Who said this?

explanation.en: Explaining what meeting Allah means, Imam Ali said it is not seeing Him with the eye but the resurrection, when God's promise of reward and punishment arrives.

anchor.quote: So the meeting here is not seeing Him with the eye; the meeting is the resurrection.

prompt.en: According to the essay, the striving of verse 6 is glossed as a struggle against which of these?

options.en: The peoples of Noah, Ad and Thamud
Satan, the enemies of religion, and the soul
The idolaters who persecuted the believers at Mecca
Poverty, sickness, and the fear of death

explanation.en: The essay reports the striving glossed as the believer's struggle against Satan, against the enemies of religion, and against the soul, which it calls one's fiercest enemy.

anchor.quote: the struggle against Satan, against the enemies of religion, and against the soul, one's fiercest enemy

prompt.en: The commentators tie the command about honoring parents, yet not obeying them into idolatry, to Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, whose mother refused all food to break his faith.

explanation.en: True. The note ties the verse, which bars obeying parents into idolatry, to Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, whose mother refused all food until he would abandon his faith.

anchor.quote: the commentators tie it to Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, whose mother refused all food until he would abandon his faith

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, how do Sunni exegetes read the testing spoken of in these verses?

options.en: As God's sifting of each believer by the strength of his faith
As a punishment sent only upon the faithless
As an ordeal that falls on the prophets alone
As proof that the faithful will never face persecution

explanation.en: The perspectives report that Sunni exegetes read the testing as God sifting every believer by the strength of his faith, the most severely tried being the prophets, then the righteous.

anchor.quote: Sunni exegetes read the testing as God's sifting of every believer according to the strength of his faith

prompt.en: According to the passage, how does the commentary link verses 14 to 22 to the surah's opening?

options.en: Proof that Noah's people repented in time
A promise that the tested are always spared
A sequel showing trial is a divine norm no one escapes
A fresh subject unrelated to the surah's start

explanation.en: The passage reads the verses as a sequel to the opening, which announced trial as a divine norm; God points to past peoples He tested, saving some and destroying others.

anchor.quote: a sequel to the surah's opening, which announced that trial is a divine norm no one escapes

prompt.en: "Noah lived two thousand three hundred years: eight hundred and fifty before he was sent ... and five hundred after he came down from the Ark." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq gave Noah's whole span as two thousand three hundred years: eight hundred fifty before his mission, nine hundred fifty calling his people, and five hundred after the Ark.

anchor.quote: Noah lived two thousand three hundred years: eight hundred and fifty before he was sent, a thousand years less fifty among his people calling them

prompt.en: According to the passage, what does Abraham give as the real motive for worshipping God?

options.en: The hope of provision from the idols
Fear of the flood that took Noah's people
The promise of long life like Noah's

explanation.en: The commentary observes that Abraham's closing words make the return to God, not the hope of provision, the real motive for worship, since provision has its own worldly causes.

anchor.quote: this last clause makes the return, not the hope of provision, the real motive for worship

prompt.en: The Prophet said of Ali in his sermon: he is the ____ of every believing man and woman after me.

explanation.en: The narration on verse 18 ties the verse to Ali, whom the Prophet names in his sermon the guardian of every believing man and woman after him.

anchor.quote: The Prophet said of Ali in his sermon: he is the guardian of every believing man and woman after me

prompt.en: According to the passage, the deniers rejected the messengers for reasons that had nothing to do with the resurrection.

explanation.en: False. The passage says these verses answer the deniers' true objection, because their rejection of the messengers rests on rejecting the resurrection itself.

anchor.quote: these verses answer the deniers' true objection, since their rejection of the messengers rests on rejecting the resurrection

prompt.en: According to the passage, verse 23 tells the Prophet plainly who will be lost, where an earlier verse had left that open.

explanation.en: Verse 23 breaks off Abraham's story to turn on the deniers; the commentary reads it as plainly naming, for the Prophet, who will be lost, where an earlier verse had left that open.

anchor.quote: Al-Mizan reads this as an address that tells the Prophet plainly who will be lost, after an earlier verse had left it open

prompt.en: Whoever acts for God, He grants his ____ in this world and the next, and suffices him in both.

explanation.en: Imam Ali teaches that whoever acts for God is granted his reward in both this world and the next, citing Abraham, who was given his reward in this world.

anchor.quote: Whoever acts for God, He grants his reward in this world and the next, and suffices him in both

prompt.en: In the passage's Shia reading, why does the honor of prophethood and leadership pass only through Abraham's purified progeny?

options.en: His reward in this world had to stay in his line
Prophethood and leadership form a single, undivided rank
The covenant does not reach the wrongdoers
The fire had spared only Abraham among his people

explanation.en: The Shia reading restricts the honor to Abraham's elect and purified line because the covenant does not reach the wrongdoers, so prophethood and leadership descend only through the chosen.

anchor.quote: the covenant of 2:124 does not reach the wrongdoers, so it descends only through the chosen line ending in the Imams

prompt.en: 'They used to break wind in their gatherings, without shame or modesty.' Who said this of Lot's people?

explanation.en: Glossing the outrages committed in their gatherings, Imam al-Rida says Lot's people used to break wind there without shame or modesty.

anchor.quote: They used to break wind in their gatherings, without shame or modesty

prompt.en: At the passage's close, how does the passage describe the people Lot prays for help against?

options.en: Those who deny the signs of God
Those who spread corruption in the earth
Those who took idols for mutual affection
Those who despaired of God's mercy

explanation.en: The passage closes on Lot's plea against the corruptive lot, glossed as those who spread corruption in the earth, its answer held for the verses that follow.

anchor.quote: Lot answers with a prayer, 'My Lord! Help me against this corruptive lot,' whom al-Tibyan glosses as those who spread corruption in the earth

prompt.en: According to the essay, why does Abraham tell the angels 'Lot is in it'?

options.en: To warn Lot to flee the town before the punishment
To turn the punishment from the town as an honor to Lot
To claim the town's people were not really wrongdoers
To ask that only his own household be spared

explanation.en: The essay says al-Mizan reads Abraham as seeking to turn the punishment away from the town as an honor to Lot, since he knew God does not destroy a prophet.

anchor.quote: he was seeking to turn the punishment away from the town as an honor to Lot, since he knew God does not destroy a prophet

prompt.en: Majma and al-Tibyan read this as plain proof against the ____, for had the wrong been God's doing they would not be the wrongdoers.

explanation.en: The essay says Majma and al-Tibyan take verse 40 as proof against the determinists: if the wrong were God's doing, the people could not be the wrongdoers who wronged themselves.

anchor.quote: Majma and al-Tibyan read this as plain proof against the determinists, for had the wrong been God's doing they would not be the wrongdoers

prompt.en: According to the essay, how does al-Mizan describe the guardianship of those who take guardians besides God?

options.en: Like the spider's house, it keeps nothing but the name
A firm refuge that shelters its people from harm
A bond God rewards for its sincerity
A house stronger and safer than it first appears

explanation.en: The essay says al-Mizan reads such guardianship like the spider's house: it keeps nothing of a house but the name, sheltering no one and warding off nothing.

anchor.quote: such guardianship, like the spider's house, keeps nothing of a house but the name, sheltering no one and warding off nothing

prompt.en: "The knower is the one who understood from God, so he acted in obedience to Him and shunned what angers Him." Who said this?

explanation.en: The passage reports that the Prophet recited the verse and said the knower is one who understood from God, acted in obedience to Him, and shunned what angers Him.

anchor.quote: The knower is the one who understood from God, so he acted in obedience to Him and shunned what angers Him

prompt.en: According to the passage, the Shia and Sunni commentators agree in reading 'those who have knowledge' as the Family of Muhammad.

explanation.en: The passage says both traditions agree the verse singles out those of real knowledge but differ on who they are: the Shia reading glosses them as the Family of Muhammad, while the Sunni keep the phrase general.

anchor.quote: The Sunni commentators keep the phrase general: Ibn Kathir takes it as those firmly grounded in knowledge who understand and ponder the parables

prompt.en: 'Whoever wishes to know whether his prayer has been accepted, let him look: did his prayer hold him back from indecency and wrongdoing?' Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked how to test whether prayer was accepted, Imam al-Sadiq said to see whether it held the worshipper back from indecency and wrongdoing; to that measure it was accepted.

anchor.quote: Whoever wishes to know whether his prayer has been accepted, let him look: did his prayer hold him back from indecency and wrongdoing?

prompt.en: According to the passage, what does 'the remembrance of Allah is surely greater' mean?

options.en: A worshipper's remembrance outweighs the prayer itself.
Remembering God matters more than shunning indecency.
God's remembrance of His servants is greater than theirs of Him.
Silent remembrance is greater than spoken remembrance.

explanation.en: The narration glosses 'the remembrance of Allah is surely greater' as God's remembering the people of prayer being greater than their remembrance of Him, not the reverse.

anchor.quote: God's remembrance of the people of prayer is greater than their remembrance of Him.

prompt.en: Tabrisi holds this is not abrogated by any later verse of ____, for arguing in the best way stays the standing obligation.

explanation.en: The essay reports Tabrisi's view that arguing with the People of the Book in the best manner is not abrogated by any later verse of fighting but stays a standing obligation.

anchor.quote: Tabrisi holds this is not abrogated by any later verse of fighting, for arguing in the best way stays the standing obligation

prompt.en: The passage argues that because the Prophet had never read or written a book before, deniers had no ground to call the Quran something he copied.

explanation.en: The essay says that because he had neither recited nor written any book before, deniers were left no ground for doubt; a reader or writer could have been accused of copying.

anchor.quote: Because he neither recited nor wrote any book beforehand, the deniers are left no ground for doubt; had he been a reader or writer, they could have called the Quran something copied

prompt.en: According to the passage, what answers those who demand that another sign be sent down?

options.en: A fresh miracle sent down from his Lord.
The recited Book is itself the sufficient sign.
The punishment awaiting those who deny the signs.
The Prophet's promise of a sign to come.

explanation.en: The essay's close says that to those demanding another sign, the reply is that signs rest with God alone and the recited Book is itself the sufficient sign and a lasting mercy.

anchor.quote: When they demand some other sign, the reply is that signs rest with God alone and the Messenger is only a warner. The recited Book is itself the sufficient sign and a lasting mercy

prompt.en: Tabrisi adds that this witness is the inimitable ____, established as being from God.

explanation.en: The essay explains that the witness of the verse is the inimitable Book, the Quran established as being from God, not a bare spoken claim.

anchor.quote: Tabrisi adds that this witness is the inimitable Book, established as being from God

prompt.en: According to the verse note, whom does the passage identify as demanding that the punishment be hastened?

explanation.en: The note names the ones asking for the punishment to be hastened as the Quraysh, the deniers the earlier verses are answering.

anchor.quote: The ones demanding that the punishment be hastened are the Quraysh

prompt.en: "Do not obey the corrupt among the kings. If you fear they will tempt you away from your religion, then My earth is vast." Who said this?

explanation.en: Glossing 'My earth is vast,' Imam al-Baqir warned against obeying corrupt kings and said that if they tempt you from your religion, the earth is wide.

anchor.quote: Do not obey the corrupt among the kings. If you fear they will tempt you away from your religion, then My earth is vast

prompt.en: According to the verse note, what occasion lies behind the promise that God provides for the animals and for you?

options.en: The rich hoarded their grain during a famine
Traders overcharged the poor for their bread
Nomads refused to store food for the winter
The Arabs used to kill their children fearing hunger

explanation.en: The note gives the occasion: the Arabs used to kill their children out of fear of hunger, and God answered that He provides for them and you.

anchor.quote: the Arabs used to kill their children out of fear of hunger, and God answered that He provides for them and for you

prompt.en: According to the essay, the idolaters' confession that Allah is the Creator leaves them free to go on worshipping other gods.

explanation.en: The essay says the proof is now complete against them: by confessing the Creator they are bound to worship Him alone, not left free to worship others.

anchor.quote: the proof is now complete against them, for by confessing the Creator they are bound to worship Him alone

prompt.en: According to the commentary, anyone who truly understood the gap between this world and the next would choose the enduring life over the passing one.

explanation.en: The essay reports al-Tabrisi's point that whoever grasped how the two lives differ would prefer the lasting Hereafter to the fleeting world, so this restatement is correct.

anchor.quote: al-Tabrisi adds that whoever grasped the difference would prefer the lasting to the fleeting

prompt.en: According to the essay, how does the commentary read the words 'Let them enjoy'?

options.en: As a genuine permission to enjoy this world
As a threat, not a permission
As a reward for their prayers at sea
As a call to give thanks on land

explanation.en: The essay says that once saved the pagans return to idolatry in ingratitude, so 'Let them enjoy' is not permission but a threat, sealed by 'Soon they will know'.

anchor.quote: the words 'Let them enjoy' carry not permission but a threat: 'Soon they will know'

prompt.en: God made Mecca a safe sanctuary while people are ____ all around it, so would they believe in falsehood and deny God's blessing?

explanation.en: The essay contrasts Mecca's safety with the danger around it, saying people are seized all around the sanctuary, so 'seized' is the word the passage uses.

anchor.quote: God made Mecca a safe sanctuary while people are seized all around it

prompt.en: "God says, 'and Allah is indeed with the virtuous' - and I am that virtuous one." Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked about the closing words 'and Allah is indeed with the virtuous,' Imam Ali identified himself as that virtuous one, so he is the speaker.

anchor.quote: God says, 'and Allah is indeed with the virtuous' - and I am that virtuous one.

prompt.en: In the perspectives, the Shia narrations apply the final verse specifically to whom?

options.en: All who merely say they believe
All the people of the sanctuary at Mecca
The Family of Muhammad and their followers

explanation.en: The perspectives say the Shia narrations give the verse a specific application: al-Baqir teaches it is for the Family of Muhammad and their followers.

anchor.quote: al-Baqir teaches this verse is for the Family of Muhammad and their followers
